title: Alignment runway & delegate accelerator — Q3 company cadence draft
content:
Purpose

Quick working draft to align leadership and key cross-functional partners on the Q3 alignment runway (12-week cadence), proposed company-level OKRs, core asks for teams, and a lightweight all-hands format that doubles as a decision forum. This is intentionally concise — surface-level + action items to convert into the more formal all-hands brief and exec memo.

Context & constraints

- We have three competing priorities entering Q3: stabilize latency SLAs for hosted API, close the Dedicated reseller pilot, and deliver the Private deployment compliance checklist for SOC groundwork.
- Hiring pressure: demand for infra/SRE headcount vs product feature work. We should avoid new heavy cross-org projects unless paired with committed FTE.
- Major tradeoff: performance (latency/cost) work moves short-term unit economics but postpones some feature-perceived value for top customers.

High-level Q3 thesis (one sentence)

"Lock in predictable inference economics at scale while shipping the minimum consented experience for Dedicated and Private customers — protect reliability, reduce per-token variability, and increase measurable adoption on Dedicated."

Proposed company-level OKRs (for discussion)

Objective C1: Make inference predictable and economical for production customers
- KR1: Reduce 95th percentile inference latency for hosted API 'small' requests by 18% (baseline: 220ms)
- KR2: Reduce per-inference token cost for 90% of requests by 12% via batching & cache improvements
- KR3: Pilot beta billing for Dedicated with 3 committed customers (>=$20k/month each) on reserved capacity

Objective C2: Harden Dedicated & Private paths for enterprise purchase readiness
- KR1: Complete Dedicated reseller pilot and convert at least 2 partners into signed letters of intent
- KR2: Ship Private v1 compliance bundle (SOC-analog checklist, KM integrations docs, initial audit playbook)
- KR3: <internal> reduce mean time to recover (MTTR) for Private deploy incidents to under 45 minutes in our staging tests

Objective C3: Keep developer velocity high while de-risking platform operations
- KR1: Stabilize the SDK surface (no breaking changes) and keep SDK rollback rate to zero for q3 releases
- KR2: Deliver 3 developer-facing observability dashboards (cost per route, per-token quality alerts, KV cache hit rate)
- KR3: Add a lightweight eval set (10 prompts per vertical) and measure regression signals across model rollouts

Cross-functional asks (owners + ask)

- Serving Runtime (owner: Marta Alvarez): Focus sprint weeks 1–4 on batching and kernel selection improvements. Deliver perf-validated patches and a rollout window to staging by end of week 4.
- Platform & Console (owner: Devon Li): Expose a per-route cost preview and a single-pane for fallback policies by week 6 for sales demos.
- Sales & Solutions (owner: Samir Banerjee): Surface 5 pilot customers who can take Dedicated demos in June and commit LOIs by end of quarter.
- SRE & Infra (owner: Ethan Cole): Work with Platform to enable a cross-region fallback policy test harness and run three simulated failovers.
- Research/Applied ML (owner: Priya Shah — collaborator): Prioritize quantization/Quality tradeoff doc for top 3 model families; deliver evaluation artifacts for KR3 of C3.

All-hands (cadence + proposed format)

Goal: use the all-hands not just for updates but for alignment decisions (one live ratification per meeting).
Frequency: single monthly sync during Q3; one longer kickoff (90m) at start of quarter, then two 60m checkpoints.
Proposed run-of-show (90m kickoff)
- 00–10m: Quick founders’ framing (one-sentence thesis + 2 asks)
- 10–30m: Compact OKR walkthrough (product & ops leads, 2 slides each)
- 30–50m: Customer spotlight (pilot demo or 5-min case) + short Q&A
- 50–70m: Decision board (present 1 decision; vote + commit owners)
- 70–90m: Org asks and blocker triage (capture action owners and deadlines)

Decision protocol (lightweight)

- Decisions that change cross-org resourcing >2 FTEs require exec sign-off and a 72-hour cooling window.
- Operational tradeoffs under threshold (<=2 FTEs, no SLA changes) can be resolved at staff+ level during the all-hands decision board with majority of functional owners present.

Risks & mitigations

- Risk: Batching changes reduce tail quality for some prompts.
  Mitigation: Canary with a 2-stage quality check using the eval set; automatic rollback on regression >5 pts.
- Risk: Dedicated pilot stalls due to partner integration gaps.
  Mitigation: Assign one solutions engineer per partner and a bi-weekly runbook; escalate to sales director at first sign of slide.
- Risk: Private compliance checklist gaps cause procurement delays.
  Mitigation: Bring in security counsel for a 2-hour rapid review and produce a prioritized remediation backlog (top 5 items).

Quick timeline (12-week runway)

Weeks 1–4: Performance & batching sprint; Dedicated pilot onboarding starts; compliance scoping for Private
Weeks 5–8: Console features for cost preview; partner LOI outreach; run initial failover tests
Weeks 9–12: Pilot convert push; audit playbook dry run; all-hands retrospective + rebaseline OKRs

Metrics dashboard (what we want 1-click on console)

- 95th percentile latency trend per model family and route
- Per-token cost breakdown and moving 7-day avg
- KV cache hit rate and prefix reuse metric
- Number of Dedicated pilot seats engaged
- Regression alerts fired on eval prompts (count & severity)

Open questions for execs (to decide before the kickoff)

1) Do we prioritize reducing cost-per-token or 95th percentile latency if we can only commit to one engineering sprint in weeks 1–4? Recommend: latency first (protect customer experience).
2) What is our minimum acceptable pilot size to mark Dedicated as "sales-ready" (3 LOIs vs 5 LOIs)? Recommend: 3 LOIs with revenue thresholds.
3) Compression: are we comfortable with a single cross-org "sprint pod" model for the first 4 weeks or prefer parallel squads? Recommendation: sprint pod for speed; rotate owners after week 4.

Immediate next steps (this doc's owner)

- Turn this draft into the all-hands brief (slides + 1-pager) by 2026-03-09 (owner: Rhea Singh).
- Run a 30-minute leadership sync 2026-03-10 to lock the three company OKRs and the decision protocol (invites: execs + team leads above).
- Create a Jira epic per OKR and tag owners; link epics to CONFLUENCE-98123.

Notes to self / rough TODOs

- Need a concise CEO talking line (30s) that threads mission -> tradeoff -> ask. Draft: "Our job this quarter is to make inference so predictable and economical that teams stop building around variance — that means fewer surprises for customers and lower unit cost for everyone. We need engineering focus on latency now, and sales to bring pilots that validate the economics. If we can do that, Dedicated moves from experiment to product."
- Prep two customer anecdotes (one Hosted latency issue solved, one early Dedicated success) for the kickoff.
- Confirm guest for customer spotlight by 2026-03-07.
